summary: Weekly POC sync focused on INT8 vs FP8 quantization tradeoffs. INT8 gives 2.6x throughput uplift with small quality regressions on long-form summarization; FP8 (mixed) preserves quality but is less stable across kernels. Agreed to run full client-side p99 latency test on Dedicated and share full evaluation artifacts.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-06-10
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (AtlasAI, ML Eng), Tom Reynolds (AtlasAI, Infra Lead), Priya Shah (AtlasAI, CTO)
Shared: https://tinyurl.com/atlas-quant-bench (performance spreadsheet), https://redwood.com/decks/quantization-poc.pdf (deck)

[00:00] Maya Chen: okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining the weekly sync, um let's do a quick round robin — names and roles, then jump into the INT8/FP8 results, arjun you wanna start with the perf summary?
[00:18] Arjun Patel: yeah sure, thanks Maya. quick TL;DR — INT8 gives about 2.6x token throughput on our infra runs, p50/p90 latency improved, p99 improved but less dramatic. FP8 mixed-precision setups kept quality closest to FP16 baseline but we saw kernel instability on one GPU type, some runs OOM'd.
[00:39] Lina Gomez: when you say 2.6x, is that on the same batch size? we usually run batch 4, latency sensitive, so batch size matters.
[00:52] Arjun Patel: good call — those numbers are with batch = 8 and continuous-batching enabled, we also ran batch=4 and saw ~1.9x. I'll put the per-batch breakdown in the sheet.
[01:08] Tom Reynolds: what GPU stack did you use for those runs? our Dedicated hosts are A100s but older gen, want to know relevance.
[01:15] Arjun Patel: primary was A100-80GB (driver X.Y), and a small set on A40 — the instability I mentioned showed up on a specific kernel path on the A40s; might be a kernel-selection mismatch.
[01:30] Priya Shah: are these Redwood Dedicated runs or internal bench infra? curious about real-world config parity.
[01:36] Maya Chen: these were run on our Redwood Dedicated bench cluster, config's in the sheet, Tom we'll give you access so you can repro with your fleet.
[01:44] Lina Gomez: okay, on quality — you said small regressions for long-form summarization. can you quantify? Rouge/bleu/perplexity?
[01:54] Arjun Patel: we primarily used a mix: ROUGE-L + human side-by-side on a 200 sample eval set. INT8 had about 2-3 point ROUGE-L drop on long-form summarization prompts, and in a blind human eval humans preferred FP16 over INT8 ~68% of the time on those cases. For shorter Q&A style prompts, differences were negligible.
[02:15] Lina Gomez: that matches what we saw in earlier tests — our critical workload is doc-summarization with 4k context. Do you see tokenization or kv-cache issues?
[02:25] Arjun Patel: we did see some kv-cache mismatch in a couple runs — appears to be a precision accumulation thing when sequence length > 3k, that's one of the regression vectors. We're log-ing examples in the sheet.
[02:39] Tom Reynolds: latency p99 is also a hard constraint for us — we target 450ms p99. How close are you with INT8 at our typical prompt distribution?
[02:48] Arjun Patel: on batch=4 with sequence mix you described, INT8 p99 was around 420-480ms depending on warm cache; there's variance. That's why we recommended a customer-side p99 run on your Dedicated infra.
[03:02] Priya Shah: any differences in token-level cost? we'd like cost per 1M tokens delta estimates.
[03:08] Maya Chen: short answer: INT8 reduces per-token compute, estimate roughly 40-55% cost reduction depending on batching and caching. We'll send a pricing delta.
[03:17] Lina Gomez: are there known failure modes for INT8 like hallucination increase?
[03:22] Arjun Patel: not a systemic hallucination increase across the board; the main issues are factuality on long-chain reasoning and output verbosity changes — sometimes shorter completions, occasionally off-by-one errors in tabular outputs. We logged representative failures.
[03:40] Maya Chen: let's surface an example — Arjun?
[03:44] Arjun Patel: sure, example in the sheet, run id r-2025-06-07-11: prompt was long doc summarization, baseline FP16 produce X (see sheet), INT8 trimmed some detail and omitted a small section. Human score dropped.
[03:58] Lina Gomez: could we use hybrid strategy — INT8 for short prompts and fall back to FP16/FP8 for long-form?
[04:06] Arjun Patel: absolutely, that's one of the rollout patterns we recommend: policy-based routing by token length or by intent. Redwood supports automatic fallback to compatible model variants.
[04:18] Tom Reynolds: what's the overhead for fallback? do we pay double for routing?
[04:25] Maya Chen: routing cost is minor compared to inference; you only pay for the variant actually executed. The fallback policy may increase latency for the first request that triggers fallback if it's a cold path.
[04:36] Priya Shah: about FP8 — you said more stable on quality but less stable on kernels, can you expand?
[04:44] Arjun Patel: FP8 in our mixed-precision experiments kept ROUGE/L and human preference close to FP16 baseline; however FP8 requires attention to kernel selection and compiler flags — on a small subset of GPUs we saw numerical instability and rare NaNs leading to failures or OOM. We flagged the exact hardware IDs and driver versions.
[05:04] Lina Gomez: is FP8 supported in Redwood Optimize recommendations? can we get recommended quant profiles?
[05:10] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood Optimize will surface profiles per workload; Arjun can push suggested quantization/scale ranges to the sheet.
[05:18] Arjun Patel: added. also included per-layer sensitivity maps for the model.
[05:24] Tom Reynolds: sample rate — how many runs per config? i'm concerned about sampling noise.
[05:30] Arjun Patel: we ran 10 seeds for each config, median and 95 CI reported. for client-side p99 we'll suggest more runs to stabilize.
[05:40] Lina Gomez: you mentioned tokenization mismatches earlier — we had an issue where our tokenizer normalization differ so outputs diverge. any quick mitigation?
[05:49] Arjun Patel: normalize at client side to match the model's tokenizer and pin model version. Also try request-level deterministic tokens (we can configure). We'll note the exact config you used and compare.
[06:01] Priya Shah: security and compliance — any PCI/PHI concerns with quantized models? does quantization change data residency/audit log behavior?
[06:10] Maya Chen: no, quantization is an execution optimization; logs/audit behave same. We'll attach SOC2 docs and the audit log configuration.
[06:19] Tom Reynolds: great. let's talk about the Dedicated test plan — steps?
[06:24] Arjun Patel: plan: 1) reproduce perf runs on AtlasAI Dedicated (Arjun + Tom) 2) run 3 client p99 tests for 48h 3) gather failure cases and send to Lina for human eval 4) decide on rollout (canary by route or token-length policy)
[06:42] Maya Chen: timeline?
[06:44] Tom Reynolds: Tom: we can provision a cluster by Monday (2025-06-16) and run through the week.
[06:49] Arjun Patel: i'll upload the harness and seeds by Thursday (2025-06-12).
[06:54] Lina Gomez: i'll curate the 3 prompt sets by Friday (2025-06-13).
[06:59] Priya Shah: who signs off on rolling this to prod?
[07:03] Maya Chen: jointly — AtlasAI product + infra + Redwood SE will sign off after the 48h pass and human eval threshold met. we'll define success criteria in the sheet.
[07:13] Audience noise / crosstalk\/murmur
[09:00] Arjun Patel: quick note — we saw 1 failing run on A40 where FP8 produced NaN mid-infer; we've filed an internal kernel fallback to force FP16 for that GPU at runtime until vendor fixes arrive.
[09:18] Lina Gomez: can Redwood auto-detect and fallback?
[09:22] Arjun Patel: yes we can set kernel safety nets; Redwood runtime supports automatic fallback to a safe execution path.
[09:30] Tom Reynolds: what's the impact on throughput when fallback triggers?
[09:34] Arjun Patel: slight hit — maybe 5-12% on that slot while fallback active; overall cluster unaffected if autoscaling/bursting configured.
[09:45] Priya Shah: good. any notes on caching/k-v cache behaviour with quantized runs?
[09:51] Arjun Patel: prefix/KV cache works but precision of cached kv can affect repetition/continuity in long sessions; we recommend revalidate with long-run conversational tests.
[10:05] Maya Chen: ok let's recap action items and owners — Arjun to upload sheet/seeds, Tom to provision cluster, Lina to send prompt sets, Maya to send pricing and security docs. Any other blockers?
[10:20] Lina Gomez: only one — we need sample human eval rubric; can Redwood provide a template?
[10:26] Maya Chen: yes will attach a rubric template in the sheet.
[10:30] Priya Shah: thanks all — if the Dedicated run looks good we'll discuss a pilot commit.
[10:35] Meeting close: confirmations on dates, next sync scheduled for 2025-06-17 same time.
